name: Cebranopadol
summary: Cebranopadol, also known by its developmental code names TRN-228 and formerly GRT-6005, is an experimental atypical opioid analgesic which is under development for the treatment of various types of pain as well as for treatment of substance-related disorders. It is taken orally.

pharmacology.text: Cebranopadol acts as a non-selective opioid receptor agonist, including as a dual μ-opioid receptor (MOR) and nociceptin receptor (NOP) full agonist and to a lesser extent as a κ-opioid receptor partial agonist. It is also a δ-opioid receptor full agonist to a much lesser extent.
pharmacology.kind: Non-selective opioid receptor agonist; μ-Opioid receptor agonist; Nociceptin receptor agonist; κ-Opioid receptor agonist; Opioid analgesic

uses.text: Cebranopadol remains investigational and is not yet approved for any medical use.

sideEffects.text: Side effects of cebranopadol include nausea, vomiting, constipation, somnolence, euphoria, and respiratory depression, among others.

fact.en: It was discovered by the German company Grünenthal, which also developed tramadol. It activates the nociceptin receptor, a member of the opioid receptor family that was only identified in the 1990s.
fact.zh: 它由德國格蘭泰（Grünenthal）藥廠發現，這家公司也開發了曲馬多。它會活化痛敏肽受體，這是鴉片類受體家族的一員，直到 1990 年代才被發現。
fact.zhHans: 它由德国格兰泰（Grünenthal）药厂发现，这家公司也开发了曲马多。它会活化痛敏肽受体，这是鸦片类受体家族的一员，直到 1990 年代才被发现。
